carossio_anchor.source_caution: MML 2013 documents a lower reach without direct open surface exit to the Rimac; do not interpret the model pour point as proof of an unobstructed surface channel.

independent_topology_support.statement_used: Juan Carossio is a distinct torrent/drainage whose lower limit delivers to the Rimac River.

predeclared_resolution_method.name: FROZEN_CASHAHUACRA_TO_MML_R4_RIMAC_D8_FIRST_INTERSECTION_WITH_CAROSSIO_R6
predeclared_resolution_method.step_1: Build a DEM domain containing the frozen Cashahuacra outlet, MML R6 Carossio and MML R4 Rimac coordinates with a fixed 0.05 degree margin.
predeclared_resolution_method.step_2: Map the frozen Cashahuacra outlet spatial coordinate to the 30 m grid and trace D8 downstream. Require the trace to progress toward and pass within two DEM-cell diagonals of MML R4; truncate at the nearest accepted R4 cell. This is the event-independent Rimac mainstem path candidate.
predeclared_resolution_method.step_3: Enumerate grid ambiguity for MML R6 and trace D8 downstream from every admissible R6 cell.
predeclared_resolution_method.step_4: Select the first intersection of each R6 trace with the accepted Cashahuacra-to-R4 mainstem path.
predeclared_resolution_method.step_5: Require all admissible R6 cells to converge to exactly one first-intersection cell; otherwise remain PENDING_REVIEW.
predeclared_resolution_method.step_6: Only after convergence may that cell be proposed as a terrain-derived hydrologic pour point for Carossio. It must not be represented as evidence of an unobstructed 2013 surface confluence; geometry freezing remains a separate step.
